    "Mean Angular Dispersion (AD) is 0.38, indicating moderate variability in heading direction relative to the ideal path.",

  ],
  "strongest_group_differences": [
    "The 'Combined' paradigm has a sample size nearly 4x larger than the next largest group ('ICMS Only'), which may obscure subtle differences in less frequent conditions.",
    "High standard deviation in Time-to-Target (2.08) relative to the mean (2.81) suggests that group means alone may not capture the full distributional differences between paradigms without checking for outliers or skewness.",
    "Path Efficiency has a very high standard deviation (0.47) compared to its mean (0.47), suggesting a bimodal distribution or extreme outliers where efficiency varies drastically within paradigms."
  ],
  "practical_interpretation": "Based on the aggregated summary statistics alone, no definitive conclusion about the *direction* of the effect of stimulation can be drawn (e.g., whether 'Combined' is better than 'Sham'). However, the high variability in Time-to-Target and Path Efficiency suggests that stimulation paradigms likely induce heterogeneous behavioral responses. The substantial sample size for the 'Combined' condition provides robust estimates for that specific interaction, whereas the 'Bright Visual Only' and 'Sham' conditions have smaller sample sizes (~3,300 and ~3,500), increasing the uncertainty of their specific performance profiles.",
  "limitations": [
    "The provided data is limited to aggregate descriptive statistics (mean, SD, min, max, n) per variable; there are no group-specific statistics to compare the five paradigms against each other directly.",
    "Sample size imbalance exists, with 'Combined' dominating the dataset (64% of rows) compared to other paradigms.",
    "The high standard deviation of Time-to-Target implies potential non-normality, making mean comparisons potentially misleading without distributional tests.",
    "No information is provided regarding the interaction between 'Mouse' ID and 'Stim Paradigm', so individual animal variability cannot be disentangled from paradigm effects."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Perform a One-Way ANOVA or Kruskal-Wallis test for each of the five response variables with 'Stim Paradigm' as the independent factor to determine if significant differences exist between the groups. Follow up with post-hoc pairwise comparisons (e.g., Tukey HSD) to identify which specific paradigms differ from each other, paying close attention to the smaller sample sizes in the 'Bright Visual Only' and 'Sham' groups."
}
